claims.claim_vi: The source groups languages into three ways of running: compiled (C, C++, Go), bytecode (Java, C#) and interpreted (Python, JavaScript, Ruby); the lesson keeps the three groups and the example languages.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: MDN: compiling transforms a program into instructions in another format or language, typically machine code; most compilers do ahead-of-time or just-in-time compilation; gcc is an AOT example invoked from a command line or IDE.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: MDN: JIT translates an intermediate representation or higher-level language (e.g. Java bytecode) into machine code at runtime, compiling frequently executed hot spots when the speedup outweighs the compilation overhead; the compiled code is executed directly by the processor; all major browsers have JavaScript engines with built-in JIT.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: OpenJDK java command: java launches a Java application by starting the JVM, loading the main class and calling its main() method.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: CPython: Python source is compiled into bytecode, cached in .pyc files so that running the same file is faster the second time; the bytecode runs on a virtual machine. Author's general knowledge, not checked: the caching normally applies to imported modules, not to a script run directly, and can be disabled or blocked by file permissions.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: CPython: Python is called an interpreted language as opposed to a compiled one, though the distinction can be blurry because of the bytecode compiler; source files can be run directly without explicitly creating an executable; programs generally run more slowly than compiled ones.
claims.verified_by: Read from a raw copy at the pinned commit in the URL (a later change to the default branch does not alter it).

claims.claim_vi: A language is not "compiled" or "interpreted" by itself; the way it runs belongs to a particular implementation.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against primary documentation.

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft: the C# compiler translates source code to CIL plus metadata; before it runs CIL must be converted to CPU-specific native code, usually by the CLR JIT compiler when a method is first called, or by ahead-of-time compilation; so for C# this step is mandatory, not optional.

design_notes_vi: Ba chuỗi bước cho ba nhóm và một khung ghi nhớ; trình JIT là bước tùy chọn với Java, còn C# có bước CIL sang mã máy bắt buộc. Lời trong thẻ viết từ tài liệu gốc, không từ câu của nguồn. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source states three clean categories and says compiled languages in general run faster than interpreted ones; the lesson keeps the three groups and examples, takes the speed remark from the Python glossary (interpreted programs generally run more slowly) and shows from the glossary and MDN that the boundaries are blurry.

Source says the JIT compiler compiles "the source code" to machine code; MDN says JIT translates from an intermediate representation such as bytecode or from a higher-level language, which the lesson follows.
The lesson explains each group from the Python glossary, the OpenJDK java man page and MDN instead of following the sentences of the source.
